pages.title: 2. COUPON, PRICE, YIELD
pages.explainHtml:
Yield 是使模型价格等于市价的折现率（对息票债常称 YTM）。它把「价格」翻译成「年化回报语言」。

Coupon ↑ → Price ↑； Yield ↑ → Price ↓； 平价时 Yield ≈ Coupon Rate
易错点：价格与收益率反向：利率升 → 旧债跌。不要把 coupon rate 当成你实际能锁定的回报。

2. Coupon, Yield,                          Price-Yield Relationship:
Price Relationship                         Inverse and convex

This means:
•   (inverse) If yield goes up, price goes down,
    and vice versa.
•   (convex) As yields fall, prices rise faster. As
    yields rise, prices fall more slowly. That is,
    the price gain from a decrease in yield is
    larger than the price loss from an
    equivalent increase in yield.
•   (convex) At low yields → bond price is very
    sensitive to small yield changes.
•   (convex) At high yields → bond price
    becomes less sensitive to further increases

pages.explainHtml:
即使收益率不变，折价债会随时间向面值靠拢（pull to par）；溢价债则逐渐回落至面值。

pages.excerpt:
3. Bond Price Change Over Time
What causes bond prices to change?
Three main reasons:
1. Credit Risk Change
    – If issuer gets riskier, investors demand higher yield → price drops.
    – If safer, yield falls → price rises.
2. Pull-to-Par (Time Effect)
    – Discount bond? Price slowly rises to 1,000.
    – Premium bond? Price slowly falls to1,000.
           All bonds "pull" toward par as maturity nears.
3. Market Yield Changes
    – Rates go up? Old bond prices drop.
    – Rates go down? Old bond prices rise.
          (They adjust to stay competitive.)

3. Price Change Over Time
  Pull-to-Par Effect: Why bond prices drift towards their face values?
    As a bond gets closer to maturity, its price
naturally moves toward par, even if nothing else
changes. Why?
This is because:
• The time value of money is diminishing, and
• At maturity, all bonds pay their face value
   (par), final price is fixed = face value,
   regardless of how much you paid for the bond.
   So, as time passes, the bond’s market price
   must converge toward that terminal cash flow.             e.g., a bond priced ￥80
Indeed, we have, in Mathes:                                  (discount), as maturity

6. Price Quotes: Clean & Dirty Price
Bond Price Quotation: What Do Those Numbers Mean?
• Bonds are not quoted in dollars — they’re shown as a percentage of par
  value (usually $1,000).
   – So 99.1 means 99.1*1000=$991.

But wait — there’s a twist with Treasuries! They use fractions, not decimals.
    e.g., How to Read Treasury Quotes: "99-05" → What Does It Mean?
Treasuries are quoted in 32nds (and sometimes 64ths):e.g.,
     Quoted Price Meaning                      Decimal         % of Par     Dollar Price*
     99-16        99 + 16/32                   99.50           99.5%        $995.00
     102-08       102 + 8/32                   102.25          102.25%      $1,022.50
     99-24+       99 + 24/32 +1/64             99.765625       99.765625%   $997.66

   The "+" means add an extra 1/64 (half of 1/32)

Dirty price（全价） = 实际成交支付的钱；Clean price（净价） = 全价 − 应计利息，是行情常用报价。

Dirty = Clean + Accrued Interest
易错点：看到报价先问是 clean 还是 dirty；算回报时用的是你真正支付的 dirty price。
pages.excerpt:
6. Price Quotes: Clean & Dirty Price
What is Accrued Interest – Part 1
• When someone sells a bond, they don’t wait for the next coupon
  payment — they get paid right away for the interest they’ve earned
  since the last coupon.
• That’s called accrued interest.

    Key Idea: The seller earns interest every day they hold the bond.
So, even if the next coupon is weeks away, the seller deserves a fair
share for the time they owned it

Accrued Interest – Part 2

How It’s Calculated:
                              Days Since Last Coupon
                       AI =                          × Coupon Payment
                              Days in Coupon Period
•   Two Day-Count Conventions:
     – Actual/Actual: used for Treasuries
     – 30/360: used for corporates, municipals
•   E.g., 6% annual coupon, semiannual $30 payments. Last coupon: Mar 1. Next coupon:
    Sep 1. Settlement: July 17.
                                        136
     – Day count using 30/360: 𝐴𝐼 = 180 × 30 = 22.67 (Coupon period = 180, July 17 to
       Sep 1 = 1 months + 13+1 day = 44 days, Mar 1 to July 17 = 180-44=136 days.)
                                                  138
     – Day count using Actual/Actual: AI = 184 × 30 = 22.5 (actual coupon period
       between Mar 1 and Sep 1= 184 days, actual days since July 17 to Sep 1 = 46 days,
       so actual days tween Mar 1 and July 17 is 138 days.)

pages.explainHtml:

pages.excerpt:
Quick Quiz

Quiz Question 1:
A bond is quoted at a clean price of 985,and the accrued interest is
12. What is the total amount the buyer will pay (i.e., the dirty price)?
• A) 985.00; B) 997.00

Quiz Question 2:
A bond has a coupon rate of 5%, but its yield is currently 6%. Which
one is true?
• A) Price>Par; B) Price < Par

pages.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
pages.explainHtml:
总结页请当成考前速查卡：能用自己的话复述每一条，才算真懂。

对照左边要点，问自己：对应公式是什么？适用假设是什么？常见反例是什么？
pages.excerpt:
Summary & Key Takeaways

• Bond pricing: A vanilla bond is worth the present value of future
  coupons and principal, discounted at the yield.
• Price-yield relation: Bond prices move inversely to yields, with a
  convex curve that favors price gains when yields fall.
• Price over time: Even if yields stay the same, bond prices pull toward
  par as maturity approaches.
• Floaters vs. Inverse floaters: Floating-rate bonds adjust coupons with
  the market, while inverse floaters gain when rates drop.
• Quoted prices: Investors pay the clean price plus accrued interest—
  the total is the dirty price.
